title: Impacket Lateral Movement Runner — DCSync, SecretsDump, and Remote Execution
goal: Add Impacket-based lateral movement capabilities: secretsdump for credential extraction, psexec/wmiexec for remote execution confirmation, and DCSync for domain controller privilege validation — the final phase of an internal pentest that proves domain compromise.
scope: Implement a 'impacket-lateral' runner in workers/runners/impacket/ using the impacket Python library (available on Kali). Three sub-operations, each requiring the highest approval gate and valid credential secrets_refs: (1) SECRETSDUMP: runs impacket secretsdump.py against a target host using credentials from secrets_refs. Extracts NTLM hashes from SAM/NTDS. Stores all hash material as encrypted artifacts only — never in findings or logs. Produces finding: 'Credential extraction confirmed on [host]' with privilege level. (2) PSEXEC/WMIEXEC remote execution: confirms code execution on target using impacket psexec or wmiexec with confirmed credentials. Runs only 'whoami' and 'hostname' — nothing destructive. Closes connection immediately. Produces finding: 'Confirmed lateral movement to [host] as [user/privilege]'. (3) DCSYNC: runs impacket secretsdump with DCSync flag against Domain Controller to confirm domain admin privilege. Extracts krbtgt hash (stored as encrypted artifact). Produces critical finding: 'Domain compromise confirmed — DCSync successful'. All three require: target in approved scope, valid credential secrets_ref, and explicit intrusive-exploitation approval. Kill switch terminates immediately.
generation_reason: DCSync and lateral movement confirmation are the proof-of-domain-compromise that enterprise security teams need to understand true risk. NodeZero includes complete lateral movement chains. Without this, AegisPT can identify AD weaknesses but cannot prove that they lead to domain compromise — the most impactful finding in any internal assessment.
